title: Have page <title> element reflect individual page titles
description:
On the tidyverse blog (and site as a whole) it seems that the `<title></title>` element (i.e. what shows up in the tab in a browser) shows up as "Tidyverse" for all pages and blog articles. The `og:title` property in the metadata is the article title, so it works fine in previews, but not in tabs. See, e.g., the difference between the tab for a tidyverse [blog post](https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2021/03/tidymodels-2021-q1/) vs. a [specific pag](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/dplyr.html)e of a pkgdown site:
![tidyverse blog post with title element not reflecting article title](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/831732/118276910-70242880-b485-11eb-87b9-27613358e485.png)
![Introduction to dplyr page with title element reflecting the specific page name](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/831732/118276999-87631600-b485-11eb-8739-a8f635deabfb.png)

Assuming this is a we'd want to make for any sites using the theme, would this go in the header partial? Happy to help, just want to make I'm working in the right direction.

cc @apreshill @hadley

title: Add CSS to style the HTML kbd tag
description:
Currently, we don't have any styling associated with the `<kbd>` tag. This might be a stylistic choice, as I've noticed we also don't use it in the RStudio [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200711853-Keyboard-Shortcuts) page, _but_ it might be nice to have some subtle effect (à la what happens when it's used on Community, or even something like [this](https://www.rgagnon.com/jsdetails/js-nice-effect-the-KBD-tag.html)).

I realized this while reviewing a post that references some keyboard shortcuts: https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse.org/pull/507#discussion_r606678168

Just as an example, on GitHub it looks like this: <kbd>Cmd</kbd> +<kbd> Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>

title: New category for blog posts: "roundup"
description:
Hello! 👋 

In tidyverse/tidyverse.org#505 we have the first of a new series of "roundup" blog posts. To quote from the post:

> We plan to begin **regular updates** every three or four months here on the tidyverse blog summarizing what's happening lately in the tidymodels ecosystem overall, as well continuing the focused blog posts on more major new features that we've always written.

We got a suggestion to make a new category for these posts. The category itself is created if I use it, but it looks like we [need a new SVG in the theme](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse.org/tree/master/themes/hugo-graphite/static/css/images).

The two suggestions we have so far are a [summary icon](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Summary_icon.svg) or maybe a [spiral](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Black_bold_spiral.svg). Thoughts?

Ideally we would get this blog post published before the end of the month. Do you think we should wait on this new SVG? Or just publish under another category?
